methodological_questions: Can lineup coverage (at least one organizer, one shaper, one terminal) be reliably measured per possession?
Is the effect of coverage separable from overall lineup talent and player counts?
Do standard talent controls behave appropriately (e.g., no post-treatment bias, no collider bias) when estimating the coverage effect?
Is there sufficient within-team variation in coverage to achieve adequate power?
Are role labels stable enough across seasons to avoid look-ahead and measurement error?

historical_evidence.finding: Named star initiators have identifiable lineup and forced-play-type suppressors in the possession graph (e.g. Jokic vs MIN lineup PPP 0.814, -0.385, n=59). Opposing DEFENSE_LINEUP ~84% coverage; min-15 gate on 8 play types.

Tests of adapter PPP lift showed an artifact: wrong-way teams did no worse than no-signal teams, and the gap did not widen with confidence. The apparent effect was produced by a construction, selection or labelling flaw.

Team offensive association structure (structural fingerprint) is more similar to itself across split halves than to other teams, even after residualizing play-type rates. Frobenius similarity S=0.352, p=0.0000; residual R^2=0.043. Wiring persistence confirmed.

Within-game and cross-game inferred defensive scheme change rates are very high (61-68%), but the near-uniform transition matrices are consistent with label noise. The inferred label cannot separate real defensive adjustment from the offense executing differently.

Backfilled play-type labels failed multiple verification checks: PNR 28.7% FAIL, PULL_UP 7.9% FAIL, 2024-25 PULL_UP ~0-2% for many teams. 82.8% of PNR labels were proxy_calibrated. Final verdict: FAIL.

Structural influence is not reducible to usage: residual share 0.906, CI [0.768, 0.962]. The usage-residual is a reproducible player property (pooled-residual rho=+0.685, p=0.0000). Both fragility hypotheses confirmed, but low measurement reliability noted.

evidence_establishes: Structural roles (organizer, shaper, terminal) are definable from usage and residual influence, and residual influence has moderate split-half stability (SF18).
Team offensive structure persists across halves and is not reducible to play-type rates (SF17).
The project possesses possession-level data with initiator, play type, points, and can reconstruct lineups.
Prior attempts to use inferred labels for within-game dynamics (scheme change, adaptation) repeatedly failed due to label noise and artefactual results (SF-APPA-001, SF-APPA-005, SF-APPA-030).
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether having all three role types in a lineup improves possession outcomes beyond talent.
Whether coverage can be measured reliably enough at the lineup-possession level to detect such effects.
Whether talent controls behave appropriately (e.g. no collider bias) when estimating a coverage effect.
How much within-team variation in coverage exists in typical NBA seasons.
own_inferences: Role labels are derived from usage and residual influence, both calculated from initiations over a set of games; applying these labels to the same games that define them creates look-ahead bias and can artificially inflate apparent effects (OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL).

To avoid look-ahead, roles must be defined using strictly prior data (e.g. previous season or first half), but then they reflect past role, not contemporaneous role, introducing noise and potential misclassification as team structures shift.

Within-team variation in coverage may be limited if teams rarely play lineups missing an organizer, shaper, or terminal; the base rate of full coverage could be high, reducing power for the contrast of interest.
Even with fixed prior roles, measurement reliability at the player level (SF18 risk MEASURE_RELIABILITY) propagates to lineup-level classification, potentially attenuating effects.
The warning from SF-APPA-005 and SF-APPA-030 suggest that any classifier built on noisy play-by-play labels could produce artefactual patterns when cross-tabulated with outcomes.
uncertainties: The exact operational definition of 'lineup coverage' (whether a single player can count for multiple roles is moot given mutually exclusive categories, but the threshold for classification (residual sign, usage median split) may be arbitrary and affect results).
The distribution of coverage gaps (lineups missing one or more roles) across teams and game situations.
The extent to which typical talent metrics (RAPM, EPM) are available for the full data window and can be included without introducing collider or post-treatment bias.
Whether 'talent control behaves' means a specific statistical test (e.g. coefficient stability, placebo checks) that can be pre-registered.

historical_effect.explanation: No prior study directly tested lineup coverage, so the decision does not rest on a previous answer. However, the consistent evidence that inferred labels (scheme change, adaptation, play-type backfill) produce artifacts and untestable results strongly influenced the assessment that role classification is too noisy for a reliable test of this question as posed.

blocking_constraints.text: Role labels (organizer/shaper/terminal) depend on usage and residual influence, which have only moderate reliability (SF18 risk MEASURE_RELIABILITY); misclassification will attenuate effects and may create artefactual patterns.

Prior work repeatedly found that inferred labels (defensive scheme, play-type backfill) are too noisy to support hypothesis tests (SF-APPA-001 artifact, SF-APPA-005 untestable, SF-APPA-030 inconclusive). Role classification inherits from the same underlying data and is likely to suffer similar problems.
Defining roles from the same season that provides the test possessions would contaminate the outcome; using prior-season roles solves look-ahead but ignores role changes and may still be too noisy.
Lineups missing an organizer, shaper, or terminal may be rare, producing small effective sample sizes for the coverage-gap contrast, analogous to the sparse player-channel cells in SF-APPA-066.
Lineups with full coverage are likely to contain higher-quality players; controlling for talent (e.g. sum of RAPM) may be insufficient due to measurement error in talent metrics and collinearity.

prior_work.summary: Earlier work established that structural influence is a measurable, reproducible player property and that team offensive structure persists across halves. However, no study has tested whether lineup-level coverage by the three high-influence roles (organizer, shaper, terminal) affects possession outcomes. Attempts to use inferred labels for within-game dynamics have repeatedly failed due to classification noise.

risks.text: Role labels are derived measures with known moderate reliability; noise will attenuate estimates and reduce power.

Systematic misclassification of players into roles (e.g. a terminal mislabelled as shaper) could create spurious coverage-outcome associations, as seen in scheme-change and play-type backfill studies.
Using the same season's data to classify roles and test coverage would artificially strengthen the association; strict temporal separation is required but may undermine contemporaneous relevance.
If most lineups have full coverage, the comparison group (missing coverage) is small, leading to low power and unstable estimates.

Coverage is correlated with overall lineup quality (talent level). Standard talent controls (RAPM, box-score metrics) may not fully remove this confounding, and controlling for them post-treatment could introduce collider bias if coverage affects the talent metrics themselves.

Coverage definitions rely on usage and residual influence, which are computed from initiations. When a key player is absent, the remaining players' initiations and usage shares change, potentially altering their assigned roles mechanically. Even with fixed prior roles, this could create a floor effect where coverage gaps appear mechanically with lower performance.
If multiple definitions of coverage (e.g. different thresholds for usage median, residual sign) are explored, false positive risk increases without pre-registration.

design.estimand: Causal effect of lineup coverage (indicator: lineup contains at least one organizer, one shaper, and one terminal) on offensive points per possession (PPP), net of opponent defense and overall lineup talent.
design.sample: NBA 2022-23 through 2025-26 regular season and playoffs (full available). Exclude garbage time (score margin > 20 in 4th quarter). Use only possessions with non-missing play-type and initiator data. After exclusions, approximately 400,000 possessions.
design.power: Pilot estimate: assuming 80% of possessions have full coverage and 20% have missing coverage, with a true effect size of 0.02 PPP (Cohen's d~0.1) and two-sided alpha=0.05, requires about 15,000 possessions per group for 80% power; available sample may be sufficient if coverage variation is adequate. However, if missing coverage is rarer (e.g. 5%), power drops substantially.
design.controls: Player talent: pre-season RAPM or EPM estimates (from external provider) for each player on court, summed to lineup-level. Opponent defensive strength: opponent season-long defensive rating or pre-game opponent RAPM. Game context: home/away, rest days, game period (1Q,2Q,3Q,4Q). Team-season fixed effects to absorb overall team quality and isolate within-team variation. All controls entered linearly.
design.falsification: Placebo test: randomly permute role labels among players within each team (preserving the distribution of labels) and re-compute coverage; the permuted coverage should show no effect. Sensitivity analysis: vary the usage median split and residual sign thresholds to examine robustness of the coverage indicator. Temporal placebo: use pre-assigned roles from season t-1 and test on season t; then swap to roles from season t+1 as a negative control (if feasible).
design.multiplicity: Single primary coverage definition and single outcome (PPP) pre-registered. All threshold variations and placebos will be reported as robustness checks with nominal p-values, not used for inference.
design.decision_rule: One-tailed t-test (or cluster-robust standard errors clustered by team-season) that coverage coefficient > 0 in a linear model of PPP with the above controls. Statistical significance threshold p < 0.025 (one-sided). Pre-registered minimum effect size of practical significance: +0.015 PPP (approx. 1.5 points per 100 possessions). If the 90% confidence interval excludes this threshold, the hypothesis is considered practically supported.
design.data_version: NBA play-by-play possession data snapshot as of 2026-07-13, including the derived play-type possession records from the graph database. Lineup reconstruction from rotation intervals and starters, cross-validated with matchup data where available.

# Terminology used in the research questions

This glossary is given identically in every condition. It defines terms only and reports no results. Definitions follow the published papers (Structural Influence; Detecting Defensive Suppression) where they exist.
